Q1: A great fire. Dated 2 Sept 1666 and titled "1666 — The Great Fire", it burns timber-built houses along the river and spreads for several days.
Q2: It begins in one small place. The baker's oven and fire in a bakery (Thomas Farriner, baker to the King) is followed by flames in a narrow street of timber houses, then the blaze grows block by block. A map later shows the burned area, with Pudding Lane and the Royal Exchange marked.
Q3: They flee on foot and by cart with bundles of belongings, and escape by boat on the river. Men pull down houses with hooks to make firebreaks. Some bury valuables in a garden pit. Survivors then camp in open fields with tents and carts.
Q4: The old church on the hill (Old St Paul's) catches fire on 4 Sept. Its windows burn and molten lead runs down the walls and across the street, and the roof burns away. The church is left as a ruin, with a toppled statue among the rubble.
Q5: Rebuilding is in red brick, with scaffolding, carts and bricklayers, and later row after row of red-roofed brick houses. The layout is the old medieval street pattern ("Rebuilding on the old streets"), not the new grand plan shown on the map. Court scenes appear as well.
Q6: A large white domed cathedral (St Paul's, with its dome finished in 1711, shown as a tall "365 ft" structure) rises above the red roofs. A tall column also appears, but I can't tell for sure which one it is from the pictures. It may be the thin column seen in the 1670s–80s aerial views, and I'm not certain.
Q7: On 29 Dec 1940 bombers and airships come over, and the city burns at night. Firefighters with hoses fight the fires, and the Gothic church burns. A damaged-area map is shown, with a "160 killed" count. St Paul's with its dome survives and stands out through the smoke and in the photo dated 1942.
Q8: A modern 2026 city of grey and glass blocks and skyscrapers, with bridges over the river. Among the towers, St Paul's dome is still visible. The film ends with a night view of lit buildings and then "how this film was made" text.
